questions.q: Describe the major relief features of the ocean floor.
answer: The floor of the ocean is not flat but has varied relief, divided into four major features.

answer.text: This is the shallow, gently sloping extension of the continent under the sea, up to a depth of about two hundred metres. Being shallow and sunlit, it is the richest zone for fisheries and also holds petroleum and mineral deposits.
Beyond the shelf the floor drops steeply. This continental slope marks the true boundary between the continents and the deep ocean.
At the base of the slope lies the deep sea, or abyssal, plain, a vast and relatively flat area covering most of the ocean floor, mantled with fine sediments.
The deepest parts are the long, narrow trenches, such as the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth.

answer: These features together make up the varied topography of the ocean floor.

questions.q: How do ocean currents form, and how are warm and cold currents distinguished?

answer.text: are large streams of water moving through the oceans along regular paths, driven mainly by winds and by differences in water density.

list: Prevailing winds push the surface water along, and the Earth's rotation curves the flow
Differences in temperature and salinity make water sink or rise, driving deep currents

answer.text: This depends on where they come from.

list: Warm currents flow from the equator towards the poles, raising the temperature of the coasts they wash
Cold currents flow from the poles towards the equator, cooling the coasts they reach

questions.q: What are coral reefs, and why are they ecologically important and under threat?

answer.text: are underwater structures built from the skeletons of tiny sea animals called corals, found in warm, shallow tropical seas.

list: They are among the richest ecosystems on Earth, home to a huge variety of fish and marine life
They protect coasts from waves and support fishing and tourism

answer.text: They are very sensitive to change.

list: Warming and more acidic seas cause 'bleaching', in which corals lose their colour and die
Pollution and destructive fishing add to the damage, so reefs need urgent protection
